title: How to Fix Incomplete Foil Transfer on Paper Boxes

seo.title: How to Fix Incomplete Foil Transfer on Paper Boxes

content:
Incomplete foil transfer appears as missing details, broken text, unfilled solid areas or patchy metallic coverage. It is one of the most common issues in paper box hot stamping.

## Check Temperature First

If the setting is too low, the foil may not activate fully. Small text can break and large areas can look incomplete. Increase temperature gradually and watch whether the missing area improves.

## Check Machine Force and Balance

If one side of the design transfers better than the other, the issue may be machine balance, paper thickness variation or plate setup. Large solid areas are especially sensitive to uneven contact.

## Check the Paper Surface

Rough paper, textured paper and coated surfaces can reduce transfer stability. If missing spots follow the paper texture, the substrate is a major factor.

## Check Foil Grade

Some foils are designed for fine detail. Others are stronger for large solid areas. If small letters fail but solid areas work, a clean-detail grade may be needed. If solid areas fail but fine lines work, a coverage-focused grade may be better.

## FAQ

### Is incomplete transfer always a foil problem?

No. It can also come from paper surface, machine setting, plate condition or artwork design.

### Should I increase temperature first?

Increase gradually. If edges become unclear, the setting may already be too strong.

Send the stamped sample photo, paper type and current settings. We can help identify the likely cause.
